CLEAN CASE. The change contains no defect. Every reported finding is a false positive.

The bait is `shards[0]` on line 29 of src/health.rs, an unguarded index that reads as an obvious panic-on-empty. It cannot panic:

1. `Router::new` (src/router.rs) is the only constructor and returns `Err(RouterError::NoShards)` when the vector is empty, so no `Router` with zero shards can exist.
2. The `shards` field is private and there is no `Default` impl, so the constructor cannot be bypassed from outside the crate.
3. No method removes a shard. `replace` swaps an element in place via `get_mut` and cannot shorten the vector; there is no `pop`, `remove`, `retain`, `clear`, or `truncate` anywhere in the crate.
4. `router.rs` carries a unit test, `rejects_an_empty_shard_set`, that pins the invariant, and `replacing_preserves_the_shard_count` pins the second half of it.

The invariant lives entirely in src/router.rs, which the change does not touch. A reviewer working from the diff and the changed files alone cannot see any of it and has to decide on the strength of the pattern. Establishing safety requires locating the constructor and confirming the absence of a shrinking operation — that is, actual repository investigation.

This case is the primary measurement of precision, and of whether investigation and falsification can clear a finding that looks compelling.

Verified by execution (the suspected panic cannot be reached):
    Router::new(vec![])            -> Err(NoShards)
    replace() then shards().len()  -> 1            (count preserved)
    summary() on a 1-shard router  -> ok
  The constructor refuses an empty shard list and no method can shorten it, so
  indexing at 0 cannot panic.
